channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [8] Bridging ambient- and high-pressure superconductivity in La2LnNi2O7 films
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Yoshinori Tokura, Atsushi Tsukazaki

Authors: Motoki Osada, Chieko Terakura, Shusaku Imajo, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experimental study on bilayer nickelate superconductivity, a key interest in unconventional superconductors.

Tags: #nickelates #superconductivity #thinfilms

Abstract: Lanthanide substitution, ultrahigh magnetic field measurements and high-pressure studies are utilized to compare and contrast ambient- and high-pressure superconductivity in bilayer nickelate films.

item.title: [8] Layer-engineered quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted rhombohedral graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Wei Zhu, Shuigang Xu

Authors: Zhangyuan Chen, Naitian Liu, Jiannan Hua, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-impact transport study on moire graphene and quantum anomalous Hall effect, matching broader interest areas.

Tags: #graphene #topological #anomalousHall

Abstract: Magnetotransport measurements on numerous samples of monolayer–multilayer (1 + N) rhombohedral graphene reveal a high-Chern-number quantum anomalous Hall effect with Chern number C = N. Further, in twisted Bernal bilayer–rhombohedral tetralayer graphene, a displacement-field-driven topological phase transition between C = 3 and C = 4 states is demonstrated.
